The two additional known/exposed roles preserve the positive-objective certificate on N-C20-U, but D takes 43.73383% more T_cert with identical U. On N-B35-S D improves supported L 0.16464% while losing U 2.24371% and enlarging signed gap about15.46345%; both stay open. These ordinary but relevant losses do not trigger the severe double-open reference rule and do not invalidate GD, yet they add no complete U/proof-speed superiority outside the selection roles. A limited candidate with disclosed tradeoffs is defensible; broad replacement or robustness is not. This is not an all-cases-must-win rule.
D.paper_conclusion: Standalone GD remains a limited uniform candidate for discussion, rather than a replacement for stable GI-TBC. Its selected-role incumbent gains coexist with new costs: N-C20-U retains the same U and accepted certificate but takes 43.73383 percent longer to certify; N-B35-S gains 0.16464 percent in supported L but loses 2.24371 percent in U, and its signed gap is about15.46345 percent larger. Both hard-role arms remain open. The new confirmation does not establish complete superiority outside selection. The same D profile is retained uniformly, with no role-based dispatch and no broad robustness claim.
